title: Theatre Studies Course
subject: listening

paragraphs.text: MIA: Hi, Rob. How's the course going?
ROB: Oh, hi, Mia. Yeah, great. I can't believe the first term's nearly over.
MIA: I saw your group's performance last night at the student theatre. It was good.

ROB: Really? Yeah...but now we have to write a report on the whole thing, an in-depth analysis. I don't know where to start. Like, I have to write about the role I played, the doctor, how I developed the character.
MIA: Well, what was your starting point?
ROB: Er...my grandfather was a doctor before he retired, and I just based it on him.
MIA: OK, but how? Did you talk to him about it?
ROB: He must have all sorts of stories, but he never says much about his work, even now. He has a sort of authority though.
MIA: So how did you manage to capture that?
ROB: I'd… I’d visualise what he must have been like in the past, when he was sitting in his consulting room listening to his patients.
MIA: OK, so that's what you explain in your report.
ROB: Right.

MIA: Then there's the issue of atmosphere—so in the first scene we needed to know how boring life was in the doctor's village in the 1950s, so when the curtain went up on the first scene in the waiting room, there was that long silence before anyone spoke. And then people kept saving the same thing over and over, like ‘Cold, isn’t it?’
ROB: Yes, and everyone wore grey and brown, and just sat in a row.
MIA: Yes, all those details of the production.
ROB: And I have to analyse how I functioned in the group—what I found out about myself. I know I was so frustrated at times, when we couldn’t agree.
MIA: Yes. So did one person emerge as the leader?
ROB: Sophia did. That was OK— she helped us work out exactly what to do, for the production. And that made me feel better, I suppose.
MIA: When you understood what needed doing?
ROB: Yes. And Sophia did some research, too. That was useful in developing our approach.
MIA: Like what?
ROB: Well, she found these articles from the 1950s about how relationships between children and their parents, or between the public and people like bank managers or the police were shifting.
MIA: Interesting. And did you have any practical problems to overcome?
ROB: Well, in the final rehearsal everything was going fine until the last scene -that's where the doctor's first patient appears on stage on his own.
MIA: The one in the wheelchair?

ROB: Yes, and he had this really long speech, with the stage all dark except for one spotlight— and then that stuck somehow so it was shining on the wrong side of the stage... but anyway we got that fixed, thank goodness.
MIA: Yes, it was fine on the night.
ROB: But while you’re here, Mia. I wanted to ask you about the year abroad option. Would you recommend doing that?
MIA: Yes, definitely. It's a fantastic chance to study in another country for a year.
ROB: I think I'd like to do it, but it looks very competitive—there's only a limited number of places.

MIA: Yes, so next year when you are in the second year of the course, you need to work really hard in all your theatre studies modules. Only students with marks get places — you have to prove that you know your subject really well.
ROB: Right. So how did you choose where to go?

MIA: Well, I decided I wanted a programme that would fit in with what I wanted to do after I graduate, so I looked for a university with emphasis on acting rather than directing for example. It depends on you. Then about six months before you go, you have to email the scheme coordinator with your top three choices. I had a friend who missed the deadline and didn’t get her first choice, so you do need to get a move on at that stage. You'll find that certain places are very popular with everyone.
ROB: And don't you have to write a personal statement at that stage?
MIA: Yes.
ROB: Right. I’ll get some of the final year students to give me some tips ... maybe see if I can read what they wrote.

MIA: I think that's a very good idea. I don't mind showing you what I did. And while you're abroad don't make the mistake I made. I got so involved I forgot all about making arrangements for when I came back here for the final year. Make sure you stay in touch so they know your choices for the optional modules. You don't want to miss out doing your preferred specialisms.
ROB: Right.
米娅：嗨，罗布。课上的怎么样了?
罗布：哦，你好，米娅。是的，很好。我不能相信第一个学期竟然快结束了。
米娅：我看到了昨晚你们小组在学生剧场的表现。非常的好。
罗布：真的吗？是啊……但现在我们不得不写一个关于整个事情的汇报，并进行深入的分析报告。我不知道从哪里开始。比如，我不得不写我所扮演的角色，是个医生，我是怎么把这个角色展开下去的。
米娅：那么，你的出发点是什么?
罗布：呃……。我的祖父在退休之前是一名医生，我是基于他写的。
米娅：好的，但这是如何运作的呢?你和他谈了吗？
罗布：他一定有很多的故事，即使是现在他也从来不说太多关于他的工作。但是他有一种权威性。
米娅：那你是如何设法捕捉到这些点的呢?
罗布：我……。我会想象他过去是什么样子，当他坐在他的诊室里倾听他的病人的样子。
米娅：好的，所以这就是你在报告中需要解释的内容。
罗布：对。
米娅：然后接下来就是氛围的问题——所以在第一个场景中，我们需要知道在20世纪50年代在医生村，生活是多么的无聊，所以当大幕拉开的时候第一个场景就是在候车室，在大家说话之前是很持久的沉默。然后人们一直一遍又一遍的说着同样的话，比如“这里很冷，是不是?
罗布：是的，然后每个人都穿着灰色和棕色的衣服，就是坐成一排。
米娅：是的，所有关于这部作品的细节。
罗布：然后我也不得不分析一下我在这个小组中是如何运作的-也就是自我发现的过程。我知道我自己在那个时候是如此的沮丧，当我们无法达成一致的时候。
米娅：是的。因此，有没有一个人脱颖而出成为领导者?
罗布：索菲亚就是。这是很好的——她帮助我们想清楚到底该怎么做，为了这个作品。我想这让我感觉好多了。
米娅：当你明白需要做什么的时候?
罗布：是的。我也和索菲亚做了一些研究。那对发展我们的方法是很有用的。
米娅：类似什么呢?
罗布：嗯，她在这些来自20世纪50年代的文章中发现了孩子和他们的父母之间的关系，或者是公众和市民之间就像是银行经理或者警察，他们之间的关系都在发生转变。
米娅：有趣。那你有什么实际问题需要克服的呢?
罗布：嗯，在最后一次彩排时一切都进行得很顺利直到最后一个场景一是医生的第一位病人出现在他自己的舞台上时。
米娅：就是在轮椅上的那个?
罗布：是的，他有一个很长的演讲，当时舞台一片黑暗，除了一个聚光灯--然后它不知怎么就卡住了，所以照在了舞台上的错误的一边……但无论如何，我们修复了这个失误，谢天谢地。
米娅：是的，那天晚上还是很好的。
罗布：但是，趁你还在这里，米娅。我想问问你关于出国交换一年的这个选择。你建议我这样做吗？
米娅：是的，当然了。能在另一个国家学习一年是一个非常好的机会。
罗布：我觉得我很想这样做的，但看起来竞争还是非常激烈的，这些地方只有有限的名额。
米娅：是的，所以明年，当你的课程已经上到第二年的时候，你需要真正努力学习所有的戏剧研究模块。只有能获得高分的学生才能得到名额——你必须证明你很了解你学习的内容。
罗布：对。那么你是怎么选择去哪里交换的呢?
米娅：嗯。我决定我想要一个项目是可以适合我毕业以后从事的工作的，所以举个例子，我选择了一个很重视表演专业而不是导演专业的大学。这都取决于你自己。然后在你要走的大约半年，你必须要把你的前三个选择发邮件给你的计划协调员。我有一个朋友错过了最后期限，就没有去到她的第一选择的地方，所以你在那个阶段就需要有所行动了。你会发现有些地方是非常受大家欢迎的。
罗布：你是否需要在那个阶段写个自我介绍?
米娅：是的。
罗布：好的。我会向最后一年的学生们要些提示……也许我可以看看他们当初是怎么写的。
米娅：我认为这是一个很好的主意。我不介意把我当时写的给你看。并且当你在国外时也不要犯我当时犯的错。我特别的投入，导致我忘记了为我回来后的一年做安排。所以要确保和他们保持联系，让他们知道你选择的可选模块。你不会想要错过做你喜欢的专长的。
罗布：是的。

Questions 21-25

Choose the correct answer.

Theatre Studies Course

questions.prompt: What helped Rob to prepare to play the character of a doctor?

options.text: the stories his grandfather told him
the times when he watched his grandfather working
the way he imagined his grandfather at work

questions.explanation: 原文中出现了三个选项中的相关内容，但是只有选项C是正确的。原文提到…but he never says much about his work...由此可以排除A;原文提到I'd visualise what he must have been like in the past, when he was sitting in his consulting room listening to his patients.“我应该呈现他过去的样子”，也就是他坐在诊室里倾听病人的样子，跟C项的意思最贴合。B项是干扰项，visualise 是“使呈现"的意思，容易错误理解为watched的同义改写。

questions.prompt: In the play's first scene, the boredom of village life was suggested by
questions.explanation: 题目问的是如何体现the boredom of village,原文中的we needed to know how boring life was in…提示下文即是答案所在。接着说people kept saying the same thing over and over,对应A项中的repetition.

questions.prompt: What has Rob learned about himself through working in a group?

options.text: He likes to have clear guidelines.
He thinks he is a good leader.

questions.explanation: 题目中的in a group定位简单，后面Rob说，I was so frustrated at times, when we couldn't agree,根据这句话可以排除选项B和C。后面接着说she helped us work out exactly what to do, for the production. And that made me feel better，正好对应A项的内容。

questions.prompt: To support the production, research material was used which described
questions.explanation: research在原文可以听到，定位较容易，接下来没有提到跟政治、经济相关的内容，可以排除选项A和C。要注意B项作了改写，shifting changing本题难度较大。

questions.prompt: What problem did the students overcome in the final rehearsal?
questions.explanation: final rehearsal 定位容易，关键是把后面的答案句听懂。原文中提到one spotlight that stuck somehow so it was shining on the wrong side of the stage，即设备故障，选B。

transcriptHtml:
MIA: Hi, Rob. How's the course going?

ROB: Oh, hi, Mia. Yeah, great. I can't believe the first term's nearly over.

MIA: I saw your group's performance last night at the student theatre. It was good.

ROB: Really? Yeah...but now we have to write a report on the whole thing, an in-depth analysis. I don't know where to start. Like, I have to write about the role I played, the doctor, how I developed the character.

MIA: Well, what was your starting point?

ROB: Er...my grandfather was a doctor before he retired, and I just based it on him.

MIA: OK, but how? Did you talk to him about it?

ROB: He must have all sorts of stories, but he never says much about his work, even now. He has a sort of authority though.

MIA: So how did you manage to capture that?

ROB: I'd… I’d visualise what he must have been like in the past, when he was sitting in his consulting room listening to his patients.

MIA: OK, so that's what you explain in your report.

ROB: Right.

MIA: Then there's the issue of atmosphere—so in the first scene we needed to know how boring life was in the doctor's village in the 1950s, so when the curtain went up on the first scene in the waiting room, there was that long silence before anyone spoke. And then people kept saving the same thing over and over, like ‘Cold, isn’t it?’

ROB: Yes, and everyone wore grey and brown, and just sat in a row.

MIA: Yes, all those details of the production.

ROB: And I have to analyse how I functioned in the group—what I found out about myself. I know I was so frustrated at times, when we couldn’t agree.

MIA: Yes. So did one person emerge as the leader?

ROB: Sophia did. That was OK— she helped us work out exactly what to do, for the production. And that made me feel better, I suppose.

MIA: When you understood what needed doing?

ROB: Yes. And Sophia did some research, too. That was useful in developing our approach.

MIA: Like what?

ROB: Well, she found these articles from the 1950s about how relationships between children and their parents, or between the public and people like bank managers or the police were shifting.

MIA: Interesting. And did you have any practical problems to overcome?

ROB: Well, in the final rehearsal everything was going fine until the last scene -that's where the doctor's first patient appears on stage on his own.

MIA: The one in the wheelchair?

ROB: Yes, and he had this really long speech, with the stage all dark except for one spotlight— and then that stuck somehow so it was shining on the wrong side of the stage... but anyway we got that fixed, thank goodness.

MIA: Yes, it was fine on the night.

 

ROB: But while you’re here, Mia. I wanted to ask you about the year abroad option. Would you recommend doing that?

MIA: Yes, definitely. It's a fantastic chance to study in another country for a year.

ROB: I think I'd like to do it, but it looks very competitive—there's only a limited number of places.

MIA: Yes, so next year when you are in the second year of the course, you need to work really hard in all your theatre studies modules. Only students with marks get places — you have to prove that you know your subject really well.

ROB: Right. So how did you choose where to go?

MIA: Well, I decided I wanted a programme that would fit in with what I wanted to do after I graduate, so I looked for a university with emphasis on acting rather than directing for example. It depends on you. Then about six months before you go, you have to email the scheme coordinator with your top three choices. I had a friend who missed the deadline and didn’t get her first choice, so you do need to get a move on at that stage. You'll find that certain places are very popular with everyone.

ROB: And don't you have to write a personal statement at that stage?

MIA: Yes.

ROB: Right. I’ll get some of the final year students to give me some tips ... maybe see if I can read what they wrote.

MIA: I think that's a very good idea. I don't mind showing you what I did. And while you're abroad don't make the mistake I made. I got so involved I forgot all about making arrangements for when I came back here for the final year. Make sure you stay in touch so they know your choices for the optional modules. You don't want to miss out doing your preferred specialisms.

ROB: Right.

米娅：嗯。我决定我想要一个项目是可以适合我毕业以后从事的工作的，所以举个例子，我选择了一个很重视表演专业而不是导演专业的大学。这都取决于你自己。然后在你要走的大约半年，你必须要把你的前三个选择发邮件给你的计划协调员。我有一个朋友错过了最后期限，就没有去到她的第一选择的地方，所以你在那个阶段就需要有所行动了。你会发现有些地方是非常受大家欢迎的。

罗布：你是否需要在那个阶段写个自我介绍?

米娅：是的。

罗布：好的。我会向最后一年的学生们要些提示……也许我可以看看他们当初是怎么写的。

米娅：我认为这是一个很好的主意。我不介意把我当时写的给你看。并且当你在国外时也不要犯我当时犯的错。我特别的投入，导致我忘记了为我回来后的一年做安排。所以要确保和他们保持联系，让他们知道你选择的可选模块。你不会想要错过做你喜欢的专长的。

罗布：是的。
